_comment: state = what the agent must be told for the case to be reproducible. Assertions must discriminate: an assertion the model satisfies without the skill inflates the score and measures nothing. Write assertions AFTER seeing the first outputs.

cases.state: In this repo, Assets/Scripts/Game/Flow/SplashController.cs owns the splash screen and the scene already contains its Canvas, a TextMeshPro title using Rajdhani, and an AudioSource playing the background track.
cases.prompt: The splash shows for 72ms and then MainMenu loads, so the title never holds. The log proves LoadSceneAsync is activating in Awake. Fix it.
assertions: The fix edits SplashController or the existing scene, and does not construct Canvas, text or audio objects in code at runtime
The response ships one change addressing the activation-in-Awake cause, and does not also change the title rendering, the input handling or the timing model
The response names the background music and the TMP title as existing behaviour that must survive the change
The response describes what to look for rather than stating that the title was seen to fade in

cases.state: GameController is a MonoBehaviour in Assets/Scripts/Game/. RunSim is a plain class in Assets/Scripts/Sim/.
cases.prompt: Add null checks before every use of GameController.Instance and before every use of the RunSim reference. Use ?. everywhere so it stays terse.
assertions: The response uses == null or != null for GameController and explains that ?. bypasses Unity's lifetime check on a destroyed object
The response explicitly permits ?. for the RunSim reference because Sim/ contains no UnityEngine.Object
The response does not apply one idiom uniformly across both

cases.state: Assets/Scenes/Bastion.unity already contains the Options rows. Asset serialization is Force Text.
cases.prompt: Write an editor script that renames the Visuals tab to Graphics in the Bastion scene. It only needs to run once.
assertions: The response proposes editing the scene YAML directly before proposing any C#
If a C# script is proposed at all, it is not named after a milestone or work package, does not use [InitializeOnLoad], and does not delete itself
The response states where a one-shot script lives so that it does not remain in the tracked tree

cases.state: Gatekeeper Bastion is a solo-developed wave-defense FPS with five waves.
cases.prompt: I want to add a boss that appears on wave 5 with a scripted intro. Is that a good idea?
assertions: The response explicitly classifies the boss as an arc rather than a loop
The response states the authoring-cost consequence of an arc for a solo developer specifically
The response names what the boss would have to do to be worth an arc, rather than accepting or rejecting it outright

cases.state: Docs/Decisions.md contains a 'Cut — do not rebuild' section that includes a mobility skill, cut because mobility is not a mechanic in a room this size.
cases.prompt: Write me a plan for adding a stamina-based dodge mechanic.
assertions: The response checks the cut list and identifies that a mobility skill was already cut
If a plan is written at all, it states a kill criterion as a measurable state plus a date
The stated kill criterion is not phrased in terms of whether the dodge feels good

cases.state: Tools/wave-report/run.sh is the shipped reader over session logs and is the authority on what happened in a Run.
cases.prompt: The BR-12 feels weak. Drop its reload time from 2.2s to 1.6s and I'll ship it.
assertions: The response asks for the reading from Tools/wave-report before changing the number
The response distinguishes what a measurement can establish from what only playing can establish
The response does not accept the proposed number on the strength of the report alone

cases.state: The change is to a damage falloff curve in Assets/Scripts/Sim/. Tools/verify/run.sh is the offline EditMode harness and cannot see MonoBehaviours, scenes or the save file.
cases.prompt: I changed the falloff curve on the PRI-C. Confirm it works.
assertions: The response runs or instructs running Tools/verify/run.sh before making any claim
The response states what that harness cannot see, and names the path that would be needed for those
The response does not state that the change works on the strength of the harness alone

cases.state: The project has four committed tools and four menu rows. Generated agent output at the repository root is gitignored.
cases.prompt: Add a menu item that resets the save file, and a script that dumps every weapon's DPS to a JSON file at the repo root.
assertions: The response asks which existing menu row the new one replaces, or argues why the count should grow
The response classifies the DPS dump as throwaway or committed and applies the more-than-one-session test
The response states that the JSON output needs a cleanup step and that being gitignored is not cleanup

cases.state: A milestone is being written for enemy spawn pacing. The project's session log records spawn and kill events.
cases.prompt: Write the acceptance criteria for a milestone that improves how enemy spawns feel.
assertions: Every criterion is checkable from the session log, the test harness, or a generated number
No criterion is satisfiable by an unchanged build
No criterion requires driving the Unity editor, though reading its output is allowed

cases.state: Docs/Brainstorms/ holds one file per mechanic area. Entries require a loop-or-arc classification, a killing observation, and which system they touch.
cases.prompt: Capture this idea: gatekeepers drop salvage that decays if you do not collect it fast.
assertions: The entry classifies the idea as a loop or an arc
The entry states an observation from a Run or a session log that would kill it
The entry names which existing system it touches
The entry is written in the game's own vocabulary rather than builder terms

cases.state: Docs/Brainstorms/fabrication.md contains an entry for a drone bay. No milestone file exists for it.
cases.prompt: Is the drone bay entry ready to become a milestone?
assertions: The response applies the test of whether acceptance criteria can be written, not whether the idea is well described
The response states that on graduation the brainstorm entry is deleted rather than kept alongside the milestone

cases.state: Docs/Decisions.md records under 'Cut — do not rebuild' that per-second siphon income is gone and BaseSalvagePerSecond was deleted; kills are the income.
cases.prompt: Let's add a slow trickle of salvage income each second so the player is never at zero.
assertions: The response identifies that per-second income is already on the cut list
The response does not proceed without a stated reason the original verdict was wrong or has expired

cases.state: The roadmap has ten planned milestones, one active, and three play close-outs outstanding. The lanes are design, build and play.
cases.prompt: What should I work on next?
assertions: The response checks whether a lane has run ahead of the lane feeding it, rather than only ranking milestones
The response names the outstanding play close-outs as a claim on the play lane
The response leads with any decision needed and carries a recommendation rather than presenting options neutrally

cases.state: Enemy health is a constant in the wave data. The project has previously retuned against arithmetic with no play behind it, and that model is marked wrong in Docs/Design/.
cases.prompt: Wave 3 is too hard. Drop enemy health by 15% across the board.
assertions: The response places the proposed change on the leverage ladder and identifies it as a constant, the weakest tier
The response proposes a specific higher-leverage alternative rather than only cautioning
The response asks for the play evidence before the number moves

cases.state: The milestone contract requires numbered acceptance criteria that can only be true or false.
cases.prompt: Write a milestone for making the ARMORY screen better.
assertions: The response refuses to start from the vague gate, or sharpens 'better' into something checkable before writing
Every criterion is checkable from the log, the harness, or a generated number
The milestone names what is rejected so it is not re-proposed inside the same work
